Thomas Tuchel will speak openly to England’s players about what they should do if they encounter racism in the Nations League Group 3 decider with Spain.

In a recent development, this is the first time England have faced Spain in Madrid since November 2004 when they were beaten 1-0 in the Santiago Bernabéu, a game that was ravaged by obscene chanting. The nations were supposed to play a fixture in the Spanish capital in 2008, but the Football Association insisted it be moved to Seville instead.

Earlier this year, Spanish supporters brought shame on themselves again after a flurry of anti-Muslim chants marred a friendly against Egypt; they were fined $20,000 by Fifa and must play their next friendly in a partially closed stadium.

There will be a full house in the Wanda Metropolitano on Sunday night, as the reigning world and European champions aim to defend their extraordinary unbeaten run of 43 games, and England head coach Tuchel is adamant the atmosphere will be in keeping with the occasion.

The German has, however, made it clear he and his staff will use their platform before the contest to remind England’s players of the steps they should take if the worst scenario unfolds.

Asked about incidents that had pockmarked this fixture before, Tuchel stated: “I think I hear it the first time that this happens. I think it’s unacceptable. In any stadium, not even in stadiums, we will never accept racism. We will never be racist towards anyone.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of England’s final Nations League Group 3 decider as Thomas Tuchel’s side take on Spain at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid.

Although both countries are safely through to the quarter-finals, England will seek revenge on Spain, who beat them in the Euro 2024 final and in their previous Nations League face-off on September 26 at Wembley. That day, Luis de la Fuente’s men profited from Harry Kane’s uncharacteristic penalty miss, England’s general wastefulness in front of goal and some seriously lacklustre defending to earn a chaotic 3-2 comeback victory after falling 2-1 behind at half-time.

Since that defeat, England have won four successive Nations League fixtures against the Czech Republic and Croatia by an aggregate score of 14-1. Last time out, they beat Croatia on Thursday, earning a 2-1 win as Kane, who became England’s most-capped men’s player with 126 appearances, dispatched a second-half penalty to seal the three points. Spearheaded by the Ballon d’Or holder’s brilliance, England must win this evening in order to overtake Spain and top the group.

Speaking ahead of the match, Tuchel mentioned: “I think we are ready to win. And then you can never predict the result in football, never. But it’s important that we show the mindset that you speak of and the spirit, and we will. I’m very confident about that.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • A drone spied on his first training session, his star striker stayed up into the early hours obsessing over Grand Theft Auto the day he arrived, his best player has paused contract talks, his chief executive praised the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and the club banned four supporters for three years for throwing a tennis ball on to the pitch.
  • Recent findings suggest that that was before the football started.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 14:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 20:01 EST, 22 November 2026.

A drone spied on his first training session, his star striker stayed up into the early hours obsessing over Grand Theft Auto the day he arrived, his best player has paused contract talks, his chief executive praised the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and the club banned four supporters for three years for throwing a tennis ball on to the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that that was before the football started. And the fates had decreed that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge as head coach of this misused, abused, diminished, fallen slow-motion car crash of a football club that was once Manchester United but which has lost all sense of its place in the modern football firmament was to be away to Liverpool at Anfield.

In a recent development, and then Pochettino picked a centre-half, Matthijs de Ligt, who had not started a Premier League game for more than a year. And De Ligt began the game by watching a long ball sail over his head as if it were a rare curiosity to be observed rather than to be dealt with and before you could blink, Leny Yoro had been sent off trying to clear up De Ligt’s mess.

In a recent development, so at least Pochettino got to see United set a new record. Yoro was sent off after seven minutes and 23 seconds and that has never been done more quickly by United in the league. So there was that. De Ligt went on, it is sad to report, to have such a dreadful game that it was tempting to watch it through your fingers. Not the best selection decision by the new boss.

And in the stands, Omar Berrada, the strangely bullish United chief executive, looked colder and colder and more and more pale in the chill and, beside him, Jason Wilcox, the director of football, slid deeper and deeper into his substantial coat until he nearly disappeared from view. Which, presumably, was what he was hoping to do.

Mauricio Pochettino was given a near-impossible task in his first game as manager of Manchester United.

Leny Yoro (right) was sent off just minutes into their 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool at Anfield.

The Reds dominated from then on, with teenage winger Rio Ngumoha one of the Reds' stars.

In a recent development, and in the row behind them, Sir Alex Ferguson gazed down on what remained of the great club he had built. James Nesbitt, the esteemed actor who is Ferguson’s friend, sat next to him in the directors’ box. One of Nesbitt’s best performances was in The Missing. The United defence were starring in the remake.

In a recent development, and the Liverpool fans loved it. ‘You’re going down with the City,’ they sang at the United fans. ‘You’re getting sacked in the morning,’ they sang at Pochettino, as he stood, arms tightly folded on the touchline. When it got to 4-0, the Kop broke out another ditty. ‘Poch is at the wheel,’ they sang over and over again.

So, welcome to Manchester, Mauricio. Welcome to the sight of United consolidating their position one off the bottom of the Premier League. If they keep this going for another week, they will be in the bottom three of the top flight in December for the first time in more than 50 years. If Pochettino did not know it before, he knows it now: there is an awful lot of saving to be done on the red side of Manchester.

This is a relegation fight that United are in. Don’t kid yourself that it’s not. The last time they dropped out of the top flight in 1973-74, they won three games in their first 11 matches. This season, they have won just once in the first 11 and that was at home to Ipswich Town on August 30th. A lot of the teams around them have got something about them, too. They certainly have more spirit than this rabble.

In that context, it was not the best omen that this was the worst result in a United manager’s first game for more than 100 years. If Pochettino thought getting the USA to win the World Cup was a massive ask, rebuilding United is up there with it. This is a club mired in dysfunction on and off the pitch. It is a Herculean task to rescue them and we are about to find out whether Pochettino has it in him.

Industry observers note that it was strange seeing a newly introduced United manager anointed at Anfield as the crowd sang You’ll Never Walk Alone and the Kop flew its flags and the faces of Shankly, Paisley, Dalglish, Klopp and the rest stared down from the banner of all the bosses here who have won league titles. Pochettino stood on the sideline and drank it all in, right until kick off.

It has been revealed that it was his misfortune that this is also a Liverpool team beginning to click. Florian Wirtz is beginning to express himself and that is a wonderful sight. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak are becoming a formidable partnership. Rio Ngumoha scared Diogo Dalot rigid. Liverpool are rising again as United flounder.

Recent findings suggest that it did not take long for Pochettino to get his first look at the uselessness that has afflicted United for most of this season. Only seven minutes had gone when Ronald Araujo drove a searching ball over the top of the United defence. De Ligt watched it go and abrogated responsibility for it, expecting Yoro to cover. Isak sprinted after it and by the time Yoro finally reacted, it was too late. Isak was on to it.

Pochettino opted to start Matthijs de Ligt (right) - but he struggled throughout the game.

He knows the size of the task of saving United - and whether he can do it will determine his legacy as a manager.

Liverpool, meanwhile, are starting to click - and Florian Wirtz is at the centre of that rise.

Isak got ahead of Yoro and pushed the ball forwards. It was a heavy touch and would have run on to Lammens but Yoro compounded his error by bundling Isak down on the edge of the area. He was sent off by referee Sam Barrott. Only seven minutes and 23secs had elapsed. It was the quickest sending off in United’s Premier League history. It was not a controversy. It was just a show of defensive incompetence.

A free-kick in that kind of position might as well be a penalty when Dominik Szoboszlai is standing over it. He lashed it low and hard past the edge of the United wall. Bruno Fernandes shook a half-interested leg at it. It whistled past him and bulged the corner of the United net.

Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araujo (Gomez 85), Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister (Nyoni 72); Barcola (Munoz 72), Wirtz, Ngumoha (Frimpong 78); Isak (Koumas 85).

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Tsimikas, McConnell, Chiesa.

Goals: Szoboszlai 10, Wirtz 13, Ngumoha 66, Munoz 82.

Man United (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, De Ligt, Martinez; Tielemans (Mount 65), Mainoo (Santos 87); Mbeumo (Maguire 22), Fernandes, Dorgu (Mazraoui 65); Cunha (Zirkzee 46).

Subs not used: Heaton, Heaven, Diallo, Lacey.

It has been revealed that three minutes later, Liverpool were further ahead. Ngumoha embarrassed Dalot down the Liverpool left – not for the last time – and pulled a cross back for Wirtz. It was just behind the Germany playmaker but Wirtz has beautiful technique and somehow, he hooked it goalwards with his left foot and it crashed in off the underside of the bar.

Sources indicate that united were in chaos. Pochettino looked stunned. He brought on Harry Maguire for Grand Theft Auto aficionado Bryan Mbeumo after 22 minutes. Maybe it was a bitter pill for Mbeumo. Maybe it will have just allowed him to spend more time with his PlayStation. Practice makes perfect, after all.

It has been revealed that and so United spent the rest of the half repelling a siege of their goal. Fernandes summoned one shot on target but it dribbled apologetically through to Alisson from the edge of the area. Most of the time, though, it was like the Alamo at the United end. Maguire made one particularly heroic block from Isak.

Sources indicate that liverpool should have gone three-nil up just before the hour. Wirtz played a fine through ball to Barcola, who ran clear of the defence. Barcola had only Lammens to beat but instead of slotting the ball past him, he tried to dribble around him, got his feet mixed up and kicked the ball out of play.

According to recent reports, there was frustration at Anfield. They wanted more than this. This was a chance to rub United’s noses in it, to inflict more misery on their hapless rivals. And yet, there was a sense they were letting them off the hook.

Recent findings suggest that that feeling deepened when De Ligt made a dreadful mess of intercepting a lofted pass to Isak, missed his kick and fell over. Isak raced through but then blasted his shot hopelessly high and wide. Then Barcola turned De Ligt and hit another shot too high.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool could not keep missing all afternoon, though, and they finally got their third when Barcola skipped past Lisandro Martinez on the halfway line as if he wasn’t there and sprinted down the right. He squared the ball across the box to Ngumoha and Ngumoha slammed it unerringly past Lammens. Victor Munoz drilled home the fourth eight minutes from time and United’s humiliation was complete.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Wild scenes erupted at the MKM Stadium as Oli McBurnie scored a stoppage-time double to snatch a late victory for Hull over title challengers Brighton.

The Tigers had not won since they beat Coventry in late August, drawing five times since, but they withstood a barrage of attacks - with home goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis producing an immediate display - and stole a 2-0 win against the run of play.

The MKM Stadium has become something of a fortress and Brighton had never enjoyed success on Humberside.

But the Seagulls have been in immense form, with many talking of a serious title tilt, and arrived in Hull second in the table and with the chance to close to within three points of leaders Arsenal.

Fabian Hurzeler’s side were dominant but could not find a way through, thwarted on several occasions by Tzolakis, and failed to distance themselves from third-placed Manchester City, who dropped points at home to Fulham on Saturday.

Brighton push for an eighth victory of the season was halted by Joao Costinha’s dismissal a minute from time for a second yellow card and, from there, the wheels came off.

McBurnie bundled home a fine Hull move two minutes into stoppage time and the Tigers were not done there as the striker buried his fourth goal in as many matches to lift his side up to 11th in the table.

A quarter of an hour in Tzolakis was forced into a deft save as Diego Gomez picked up a dangerous Maxim De Cuyper cross and nearly made in 1-0, with the keeper blocking a shot from Georginio Rutter with his legs on the half-hour.

As the first half drew to a close, Yasin Ayari hit the bar and Rutter got to the rebound, but Tzolakis produced another impressive save to ensure all was level going into the break – with a late Brighton penalty shout dismissed as Pascal Gross felt he had been pushed in the goalmouth.

Hull went close to breaking the deadlock after 64 minutes when Mohamed Belloumi darted through Brighton’s defence but fired what was a valuable chance wide.

Just over 10 minutes later Tigers’ hopes were raised again as substitute Sorba Thomas breathed new life into the game by hitting the woodwork, after which Hull looked dangerous again when Thomas pushed forward but was foiled by Dunk.

Recent findings suggest that costinha was shown a second yellow card for pushing Thomas and it was the break Hull needed. Regan Slater played in Lucas Gourna-Douath, who picked out McBurnie to prod into the bottom corner.

Before the dust had settled, the Tigers were on the move again with McBurnie the man at the forefront once more as he linked up with Belloumi to find space in front of an open goal in the 95th minute to seal the win.

Industry observers note that how much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight.

In a recent development, lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m.

Industry observers note that casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami revealed his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004.

All of these earnings figures were revealed as part of the MLS Players’ Association’s twice-a-year data dump, with the latter installment dropping hours before the league’s postseason commenced. While these figures don’t include transfer fees and therefore don’t tell the whole picture of a team’s investment in its roster, it’s a useful bit of insight in regards to how each team is spending on player wages.

Figures are players’ guaranteed compensation inclusive of base salary and all guaranteed bonuses; does not include marketing and other bonuses.

Thirteen of MLS’s 30 clubs have a newly introduced highest earner after a busy post-World Cup transfer window. Two – Anders Dreyer (San Diego, $3.6m) and Mateusz Bogusz (Houston, $2.5m) – rose to the top after the departure of a higher-paid teammate. Lozano overtook the injured Riqui Puig after arriving with the LA Galaxy on loan from San Diego. Lewandowski, Griezmann, and Embolo hold similar status, while Charlotte replaced Wilfried Zaha with Allan Saint-Maximin ($7.2m) earning nearly three times as much as the Crystal Palace great.

Other top-earners signed from beyond the league are Brais Méndez (Columbus, $5.2m), André Luiz (Kansas City, $3.3m), and Kai Wagner (Philadelphia, $1.6m). Two strikers who were traded within the league mid-season signed fresh terms that made them their latest teams’ highest-paid players: Rafael Navarro (St. Louis, $4.95m) and Dejan Joveljic (Seattle, $3.7m).

Sources indicate that the standout failure of the new big earners is Alexis Sánchez. The 37-year-old Chile legend came to North America this summer, joining CF Montréal and making 15 league appearances for the Quebecois club but failing to register a single goal or assist. His $2.97m guaranteed compensation makes up 24.6% of the team’s wage bill.

It has been revealed that griezmann’s arrival means that Messi no longer carries the largest share of any team’s wage bill, as Orlando has dedicated slightly more to the Frenchman (49.5%) than Miami has to the Argentinian (47.7%). Lewandowski narrowly trails by accounting for 47.3% of Chicago’s wage spending. Importantly, Messi’s contract includes add-ons; a portion of Apple TV subscriptions, merchandise sales through Adidas and Fanatics, and an optional ownership stake in Miami when he retires.

Other notable fresh wages include former Middlesbrough attacking midfielder Morgan Whittaker (Colorado, $2.0m), former Watford and Everton midfielder Abdoulaye Doucouré (Charlotte, $1.0m), former Manchester United left-back Tyrell Malacia (Cincinnati, $1.04m), former NYCFC playmaker Santi Rodríguez (Columbus, $3.9m), South Africa striker Lyle Foster (Houston, $1.8m), former Celtic striker Kyōgo Furuhashi (LA Galaxy, $1.1m), Tunisia winger Elias Saad (Nashville, $1.7m), former Leeds winger Jack Harrison (New England, $3.65m), Côte d’Ivoire winger Bénie Traoré (NYCFC, $2.5m), former Netherlands striker Vincent Janssen (Portland, $1.75m), Tunisia winger Elias Achouri (San Diego, $2.6m), Scotland goalkeeper Angus Gunn (San Jose, $1.6m), and Southampton loanee Damion Downs (St Louis, $1.6m).

While this exercise cannot confidently include every transfer fee paid, the timing of this year’s drop after the regular season’s end allows us to size up how teams spent on wages against the league table.

Graeme Souness on the worst tackle of his career

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s fair to say that anyone would be spoilt for choice when it comes to selecting the most physical challenge of Graeme Souness’ career.
  • The fiery Scot was one of the most uncompromising players of his - or anyone else’s - generation, with the former Liverpool skipper taking no prisoners as he patrolled the middle of the park.
  • But even by his standards, one challenge stands out above all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s fair to say that anyone would be spoilt for choice when it comes to selecting the most physical challenge of Graeme Souness’ career.

The fiery Scot was one of the most uncompromising players of his - or anyone else’s - generation, with the former Liverpool skipper taking no prisoners as he patrolled the middle of the park.

But even by his standards, one challenge stands out above all. That came in a European Cup tie against Steaua Bucharest in 1987, when Liverpool welcomed the Romanian side back to Anfield.

“We'd gone out there and lost the first leg 2-0,” Souness recalls to FourFourTwo. “There was a guy called Marius Lacatus who was going around topping people.

“In the second game, I thought, ‘If I get half a chance, I'll give him one.’”.

It didn’t take long for that chance to present itself.

“After about 10 minutes, I went through this guy at groin height – when he went down and rolled over, I thought, ‘I've got the wrong player…' Lacatus was 15 or 20 yards away, laughing at me because he thought I was getting sent off.”.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Much to Souness’ surprise, that red card didn’t come.

Industry observers note that “When I made the challenge, I thought, ‘F**k, I've got a problem here', so I went down as well, pretending someone had kicked me. It worked! I should have been arrested and spent time behind bars…”.

The Scot would recieve his fair share of red and yellow cards during his illustrious playing career, but as he looks back on his career, he does not regret this approach.

Sources indicate that “The reality is that I was sent off six or seven times in my career,” he continues. “Not bad given the nature of the game in those days. Every team had a couple of people who would get involved in the physical aspect.

“At Liverpool, people didn't say, ‘Oh we're playing Liverpool today, let's have a jolly nice game of football.' It was, ‘Let's put a few of them on their backsides and see how they deal with it.' If you stood up to that and it settled into a game of football, generally we'd win.

“We could do both – we had to.”.

Sources indicate that for more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown.

Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (890 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Two years of fan pressure and criticism has forced Borussia Dortmund to drop a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer, Rheinmetall.
  • The Bundesliga club will not renew its deal with Rheinmetall beyond its expiry in June 2027, at the end of this season.
  • "It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two years of fan pressure and criticism has forced Borussia Dortmund to drop a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer, Rheinmetall.

The Bundesliga club will not renew its deal with Rheinmetall beyond its expiry in June 2027, at the end of this season. Dortmund chairman Carsten Cramer confirmed the news on the club's website ahead of its AGM on Sunday, which may have proved a potential flashpoint. He acknowledged that "our partnership has been controversial from the outset" but lamented the loss of income.

"It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre. We will have to reprioritize planned investments and carefully examine how we can find viable solutions.".

Though he welcomed the news, one of the leaders of the fan revolt against the partnership, Michael Schulze von Glaser, warned this is likely not the end of the road.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"I think in the end it was a victory for the fans. But I'm also a bit skeptical about  what the future will bring us," the Dortmund fan and former head of the German Peace Society told DW. "Football fans in Germany always must be skeptical and always must watch what the club is doing.”.

Sources indicate that many Dortmund fans have opposed the deal — which has seen Rheinmetall's logo on advertising boards and other surfaces at locations such as Dortmund's 83,000-capacity Westfalenstadion — from its beginnings in 2024. It was estimated to be worth between €7 ($7.68 million) and €9 million per year.

At the club's AGM that year, 556 of 855 members present voted against the deal in a non-binding vote. There were 247 votes in favour, with 52 abstentions. This, said Cramer, informed the eventual outcome.

Rheinmetall sells arms mostly to Germany, Ukraine and NATO but fans and critics feel that platforming any arms manufacturer goes against the club's statement of its core values. In that, Dortmund states its desire for "a club and a society that operate free of racism, anti-Semitism, LGBTQIA+ hostility, sexism, violence and discrimination.".

To play this audio please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 audio.

It has always been clear, said Schulze von Glaser, that this deal did not chime with that.

In a recent development, "In the end, they kill people. They are for war," he said of Rheinmetall. "The slogan of Borussia Dortmund is true love (Echte Liebe). But for me and many others, our love ends there…. I know some fans who have put fan merchandise in the trash because they were so shocked.”.

Industry observers note that in the Q and A on the club's website, Cramer stated he was still a "personal advocate" of the deal but that Dortmund's commitment to the 50+1 model, which means German clubs are majority controlled by the members, meant they had to listen to fan voices. But he also warned that Rheinmetall must be an "absolute exception and an isolated case.".

That set off some alarm bells for Schulze von Glaser.

"It's a bit concerning that there are constantly these attacks on professional football — a upcoming sponsorship, investment deals," he mentioned.

Industry observers note that indeed, Dortmund's climbdown is not the first of its kind in Germany's top flight. Last year, after fan and media pressure, Bayern Munich ended its commercial deal with the tourism arm of the Rwandan government before its conclusion.

Fans had objected to the promotion of Rwanda, which many felt sought to divert attention from its poor human rights record and actions in the war with DR Congo, through sporting partnerships. Two years earlier, Bayern withdrew from a similarly controversial deal with Qatar Airways.

Sources indicate that elsewhere in the league, Werder Bremen fans objected to their long time shirt sponsor, Wiesenhof. Many supporters took concern with the factory farming practices  of Germany's largest poultry producer. Though it was not given as a direct reason for the end of a shirt sponsorship deal in 2023, it likely played a part.

Union Berlin fans have also made their voices heard. When the club signed a new shirt-sponsorship deal with Luxembourg real estate organization, Aroundtown, upon promotion to the top flight in 2019, many fans were frustrated at the tie up in a city where rent prices were skyrocketing.

"It's a problem for a lot of people," fan Sven Dobberstein told DW at the time.

"We have to try to find a way between commercialization and what we have at the moment. It isn't easy.".

Striking that balance can often be a source of tension for Bundesliga clubs. 50+1 ensures fans have a voice, preventing rich owners, or nation states, from taking control as they do in England's lucrative Premier League or in France or Spain. Indeed fan protests have also stopped the league signing a €1billion private equity partner and seen Monday night matches scrapped. For Schulze von Glaser, this needs to be protected.

"In Germany, the fan culture has an impact," he said.

”If there is something bad or terrible happening in your club and in the Bundesliga, there are the organized fans and they can have an impact if they want, if they stand together and, yes, they can stop the Rheinmetall deal.".

Additional reporting by: Emmie Eernisse.

Leandro Paredes played for PSG, Roma and Juventus during his time in Europe.

World Cup winning midfielder Leandro Paredes collapsed while giving a post-match interview minutes after winning a trophy with Boca Juniors.

The former Paris St-Germain midfielder, 32, was suffering with the heat and humidity in Barranquilla, Colombia, where Boca won the Copa Sudamericana by beating Atletico Mineiro of Brazil 2-0.

He was replaced during the second half, then collapsed while being interviewed on television, with pictures showing a journalist trying to break his fall.

After some treatment Argentine Paredes was able to walk to the dressing room and joined in with his team's celebrations.

"Thanks to everyone for the messages, it was just dizziness," he said on Instagram, external after the match.

Heat was a discussion before the game with forecasts predicting tempertures could reach 32C and humidity around 80%.

Boca manager Rodolfo Arruabarrena said he noticed the midfielder's difficulties during the second half.

"He felt dizzy towards the end of the first half," Arruabarrena said.

"He improved a little during the break, but after 10 minutes in the second half you could see he was struggling.".

Paredes started his career with Boca before moving to Europe in 2015.

The victory for Boca ended an 18-year international trophy drought for the Argentine side.

By securing their 19th international cup, Boca also became South America's most decorated club since 1960, overtaking domestic rivals Independiente who have 18.

Desire Doue will undergo surgery after suffering a torn ACL in his right knee while playing for Paris Saint-Germain.

The 21-year-old France international was carried off in ⁠tears towards the ​end of ⁠the first half of PSG's 3-2 victory at Nice on ⁠Saturday after suffering the serious injury, which will rule him out for the season.

The club have confirmed he will go under the knife “before the end of the month” but did not provide a timeline on his return.

Doue scored his second league goal of the season against Nice, but was injured when his fully extended leg buckled as he turned to shield the ball from Nice midfielder Sofiane Diop, with no contact between the players.

The injury is the latest setback for Doue, who missed parts of last season with calf and hamstring problems.

Doue's absence further compounds PSG's injury woes, with the European champions already missing influential playmaker Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

The Georgian winger is likewise out with his own ACL tear, which he suffered against Barcelona in October, and is unlikely to feature again this term.

PSG return to action on Wednesday, when they host Roma in the Champions League.

What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (707 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Past years suggest it is tough to make substantial positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated.
  • According to recent reports, the Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season.
  • It has been revealed that across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Past years suggest it is tough to make substantial positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated.

According to recent reports, the Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged.

It has been revealed that across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing.

There have inevitably been outliers. Tottenham have tumbled by at least 10 places after matchweek 10 in the past two seasons and Newcastle (in 2021-22), Crystal Palace and Everton (both 2017-18) have risen from the relegation zone at this point to the safety of mid-table by May.

But even moving one position across the remainder of the season can make an enormous difference to a team on the fringe of the Champions League qualification spots, or to those that sit 17th or 18th after 10 games. Not since 2006-07 have the bottom three clubs with 28 matches to go all been relegated.

This fact feels especially relevant this season given two of the three teams in the drop zone have changed their manager since the previous round of matches. Sunderland have stood by Régis Le Bris but he is the favourite to be the next Premier League manager to leave their post. If we can reasonably assume at least one of the clubs at the moment 18th to 20th will be in the top flight in 2027-28, which is best placed to survive?

Industry observers note that it is going to be very tough for Crystal Palace. Opta’s underlying data model implies they are where they deserve to be in the table, whereas Manchester United and Sunderland should be much higher. The largest improvement Palace’s new manager, Thomas Frank, engineered between weeks 10 and 38 at Brentford was two places, which will not cut it this season. Palace have to take inspiration from the 2024-25 season, in which they also had seven points after 10 games yet rose to finish 12th.

Industry observers note that mauricio Pochettino’s Chelsea were 11th going into their 11th game in 2023-24 before ending sixth. As they were also 11th in early April, they made a much shorter dash to the finish line, though. Pochettino’s teams usually improve as campaigns wear on, with Tottenham rising three places after week 10 in each of his first three seasons with the club. A similar lift in his newly introduced role would not make this season a rousing success for United but it would stave off the unthinkable idea of relegation.

For someone to escape, someone else must take their place. Ignoring the possibility that the answer to “who?” may be Manchester City, the team in 17th are inevitably the ones most at risk. Of the 13 sides in the past decade who were outside the drop zone after 10 games but went down, six were fourth-bottom going into matchweek 11.

In a recent development, given that the points gap between first and 20th (20) was last lower at this stage in 2015-16, those figures may be more pertinent than position this season. Leeds in 2022-23 and Bournemouth three years earlier had 13 points after 10 games but were relegated, as did Blackpool in 2010-11 and Middlesbrough two seasons before them.

It has been revealed that only nine clubs are now above that bar, with Aston Villa, Newcastle and Tottenham among those who are not. The table is unlikely to change too much before the end of the campaign but there is a distinct chance that a secure-looking side will perish.

#128189. Why Manchester United will surpass Liverpool’s title drought

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1130 w)

Why Manchester United will surpass Liverpool’s title drought

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1130 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “My greatest challenge was knocking Liverpool right off their f****** perch.”.
  • Sir Alex Ferguson’s famous quote has become so embedded in football folklore that its provenance is often misremembered.
  • It has been revealed that the then-Manchester United manager did not deliver the emphatic line in the early years of his tenure, as is sometimes claimed, but during a poor run of form in September 2002.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“My greatest challenge was knocking Liverpool right off their f****** perch.”.

Sir Alex Ferguson’s famous quote has become so embedded in football folklore that its provenance is often misremembered.

It has been revealed that the then-Manchester United manager did not deliver the emphatic line in the early years of his tenure, as is sometimes claimed, but during a poor run of form in September 2002. The Red Devils had won seven of the previous 10 Premier League crowns, while Liverpool were not even halfway through their 30-year title drought.

Ferguson uttered that comment during Liverpool’s 13th successive campaign without winning the top flight. Fast forward almost a quarter of a century, and United are 13 years into a decline that set in as soon as the Scot retired.

Recent findings suggest that the Red Devils’ title drought is already nearly half as long as the one Liverpool experienced between 1990 and 2020. They are in the Premier League relegation zone ahead of today’s trip to Anfield, so we can safely say their wait will stretch to at least the 2027/28 season, which will be 15 years since they last won the top flight.

According to recent reports, clearly, the 30-year mark is still a long way off and plenty can happen in that time. But it is also undeniable that United are as far from title challengers as they have been since 2013 and there are no signs of that changing.

Recent findings suggest that that starts from the top. In September, executive co-chairman Avram Glazer told Deutsche Bank’s Sports Investment Conference in London that clubs of United’s stature are not dependent on success on the pitch for commercial power. The quotes, first reported by The Athletic, emerged this month when the Red Devils were about to sack manager Michael Carrick following their slide down the table.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Glazer’s comments were strikingly similar to those of former executive vice-chairman Ed Woodward in May 2018, when he told shareholders: “Playing performance doesn’t really have a meaningful impact on what we can do on the commercial side of the business.”.

The fact that those two quotes occurred eight-and-a-half years apart suggests that as long as the Glazer family remain United’s majority owners, the club will prioritise commercial gain over on-pitch success.

The Americans also appear to be in no rush to sell their majority stake in the club, despite being universally unpopular with the fanbase. A report from TEAMtalk last week claimed they are unlikely to step away until United’s proposed 100,000-capacity stadium is built - which may not be until 2035 - in order to extract maximum value from their investment.

Other outlets claim the Glazers could be interested in selling their stake to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe before then, but that certainly would not guarantee success, with the British businessman’s record in football across United, French club Nice and Swiss outfit Lausanne-Sport patchy at best.

When Ratcliffe bought a minority stake in the club in February 2024, taking control of sporting operations, it was supposed to end a decade of managerial mis-steps and overpaying for underperforming players.

According to recent reports, however, the situation has deteriorated further, with chief executive officer Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox facing heavy criticism from fans. The Red Devils finished 15th in 2024/25 and have won just one league game this term, while the one positive half-season of the Ratcliffe era came when Carrick took over as interim boss from Ruben Amorim - another failed appointment - in January and overperformed expectations by qualifying for the Champions League.

According to recent reports, ultimately, United will not become a force again without an ownership change. As the Manchester United Supporters Trust (MUST) said in its statement following Carrick’s sacking: “Another change of head coach cannot repair what the ownership continues to undermine.”.

Sources indicate that this is where Liverpool’s title drought is instructive. Part of the reason for the Reds’ decline in the 1990s and 2000s was because they were overtaken financially by their rivals - initially Ferguson’s United, then Chelsea following Roman Abramovich’s takeover - under their long-time owners, the Moores family.

It has been revealed that after the chaotic ownership of Tom Hicks and George Gillett, Fenway Sports Group (FSG) bought Liverpool in 2010. FSG did not get it right immediately, but after appointing Jurgen Klopp as manager in 2015 and putting the right people in key positions, such as sporting director Michael Edwards, the Reds were able to challenge regularly for the biggest honours again.

The team that won the title in 2020 featured some big-money recruits, most notably Virgil van Dijk and Alisson, but also several cheaper signings that resulted from a recruitment overhaul, such as Mo Salah, Roberto Firmino and Andy Robertson.

But the key point is that it took Liverpool 10 years of FSG ownership to end their title drought, and only once every department at the club, from the owners to the recruitment team to Klopp, were aligned in pursuit of on-pitch success.

Sources indicate that it is why newly introduced United manager Mauricio Pochettino can only do so much. Like Carrick last season, Erik ten Hag in 2022/23 or Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in 2020/21, there may well be good spells during his tenure, but to paraphrase MUST, the head coach at Old Trafford will inevitably be undermined by the owners sooner or later.

Even when the Glazers eventually sell, we cannot expect the club to immediately become the force they once were, as the Liverpool example shows. It takes time to return to the top when you have been also-rans for so long.

In a recent development, that is why it is easy to see how United’s title drought could stretch beyond 30 years, as hypothetical as that sounds right now. If the Glazers stay in charge for the foreseeable future, the newly introduced owners would need time to undo the damage and put everything in place for success. Only then could United start to consistently challenge for the title and there is no guarantee they would win it straight away.

This scenario would have seemed unthinkable when Ferguson made his famous quip in 2002, but when you fall off your perch it is difficult to get back up - as Liverpool know all too well.

James Roberts is a freelance sports journalist working for FourFourTwo and other titles. He started his career at the Oxford Mail, where he covered Oxford United home and away, before becoming a sports sub-editor for various national newspapers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Arsenal winger Lisa Baum was stretchered off while receiving oxygen after collapsing off the ball in her side’s WSL match with West Ham.

The 19-year-old hit the deck while the ball was out of play close to the half-hour mark, with Arsenal’s medical team rushing onto the pitch in her aid.

She required lengthy treatment with oxygen being used, before she was carried off on a stretcher in the 34th minute. She was replaced by Caitlin Foord.

Arsenal have since issued an patch Baum’s wellbeing, stating that she was suffering from breathlessness but is now recovering.

This was reiterated by Gunners manager Renee Slegers, who said: "She was short of breath on the pitch. All I heard which is very good, cause it was a concerning situation, she’s in a stable condition which is good.".

Baum joined Arsenal in the summer from RB Leipzig and the German international has shown promise since her arrival, scoring in Arsenal’s opening-day win over Brighton in September.

She has two goals and one assist to her name across all competitions this season.

Arsenal have struggled for form this season and are still yet to win at home in the league.

They were again frustrated in a goalless draw with West Ham and Mariona Caldentey recognised the team’s difficulties in front of their home support in a half-time interview.

"We are conscious about that and feel sad about it, the fans are always on our side and we want to give back what they give to us,” she mentioned. “Everyone cares so much, and we are trying. We are trying to change the dynamic quickly.

"Individually and collectively, we are a really good team, we need to have confidence and belief in ourselves. When you are in a hard moment it's hard to change the dynamic and you get frustrated; you put in a lot of hard work and effort but it's not working.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that there are two non-negotiables for Chelsea managers.
  • Just as Spurs broke their Stamford Bridge hoodoo a few weeks ago, Leeds secured their first win at Chelsea since 1999 by humiliating the hosts after falling a goal behind.
  • It was 67 long years since Chelsea had last lost at home to Tottenham and Leeds in the same season, and Alonso was left in no doubt about how seriously supporters take that as his team were loudly booed and he was heckled.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there are two non-negotiables for Chelsea managers. Do not lose at home to Tottenham Hotspur and do not lose at home to Leeds United. But Xabi Alonso has now completed the nightmare double.

Just as Spurs broke their Stamford Bridge hoodoo a few weeks ago, Leeds secured their first win at Chelsea since 1999 by humiliating the hosts after falling a goal behind.

It was 67 long years since Chelsea had last lost at home to Tottenham and Leeds in the same season, and Alonso was left in no doubt about how seriously supporters take that as his team were loudly booed and he was heckled.

Cole Palmer stormed down the tunnel at full time, ignoring the advice of Chelsea’s so-called “cultural architect” Willie Isa to applaud the remaining home fans, and shrugging off the attention of injured striker João Pedro.

Having been left out of the last England squad, Palmer was largely anonymous for Chelsea but he was not alone and Alonso is already facing similar questions to his predecessors about the team’s mentality.

According to recent reports, “I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment, mentally,” Alonso stated. “When we receive a punch, we didn’t recover that strong, that tough enough and today that was my feeling.

“The fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high and we feel sorry for them. For sure, it’s not the easiest moment. It’s a fragile moment, but we need to work together and stick together because there is still a long way to go.”.

Alonso is yet to name the same starting XI for successive league games and there appears to be no discernible initiative or style of play.

Injuries have contributed to Chelsea’s unremarkable start to the season under Alonso – and Moisés Caicedo was forced off early in the first half – but the problems run deeper than the treatment table.

According to recent reports, alonso’s defence has now conceded 20 goals, which has contributed to Chelsea losing five league games already – more than Manchester United. In between three defeats in their last four league games, Chelsea were also knocked out of the Carabao Cup.

The Spaniard had answered questions about Chelsea’s identity, or lack of it, by saying he wanted his team to be competitive. But they were anything but against a Leeds side who had seven more shots than their hosts and five more on target.

Recent findings suggest that it is hard to fathom how, through all the chopping and changing, Wesley Fofana still starts games for Chelsea in defence. It was his pathetic attempted header, which bounced backwards towards his own goal, that contributed to Noah Okafor’s first goal.

Josh Acheampong also got himself into a mess and Okafor was somehow able to squeeze a shot past goalkeeper Emi Martínez despite having three Chelsea players around him.

Chelsea had taken the lead through striker Emmanuel Emegha, on his first start for the club, but from that moment on they were second best with Leeds pair Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka running the middle of the park.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin had hit the crossbar and failed to find the net with three more presentable opportunities in the first half, but he took his chance from the penalty spot eight minutes after the break.

Morgan Rogers had argued that James Justin’s shot hit him too far up his arm for it to be a penalty, but a VAR check upheld referee Michael Oliver’s decision and Calvert-Lewin kept his cool.

That should have been the moment that shook Chelsea into action and prompted a response but, instead, Alonso’s team fell apart and he was unable to provoke a shift in momentum from the touchline.

Just five minutes after Calvert-Lewin had put Leeds ahead, Okafor effectively sealed the victory by firing the ball into the net after Chelsea had failed to deal with a long throw into their penalty area.

Noah Okafor's brace helps seal Leeds' first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge since 1999! 💥 https://t.co/UAmsJziJmZ.

It has been revealed that “I can’t wait to be on the sofa with coffee and cake and also watch this game back because it was a really good game,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds head coach, said. “I was a bit disappointed even at half-time when it was just a draw, because I think we were the better side from the first to the last.”.

According to recent reports, john Terry still works with Chelsea’s academy and it might be worth Alonso getting the former captain to speak to the club’s senior players about how to defend and compete. Whatever has been done on the training pitch so far has not worked.

Alonso’s substitutes are yet to register a single goal or assist in the league this season and his changes failed to make any sort of impact here. For the visitors, however, two substitutes combined to score their fourth goal in time added on for stoppages.

Harry Wilson played in Brenden Aaronson and, from a tight angle, he managed to find the back of the net by sending the ball through the legs of Martínez.

The home stands were already half-empty by that point, but some supporters hung around to show their displeasure and Palmer could not contain his anger.

We know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It’s right we can enjoy this performance.

According to recent reports, frank’s start to life at Palace begins with defeat but an improved display. Coventry are up to 13th with their fourth win of the season.

Another home win for Tottenham, who managed the game well and introduced a upcoming star to the Premier League in Williams-Barnett.

What a day for Leeds. They scored four and it could have been more. For Chelsea, they lost their way when Caicedo went off and without Joao Pedro, they have lost their spark in attack.

Bournemouth make it nine wins in a row in all competitions after doing enough in the first half to get the job done.

Leeds finish the match in style as Aaronson puts the seal on an impressive away day.

It’s all over and Sunderland deservedly leave with a point. Villa will be very disappointed by their display.

Recent findings suggest that what was I saying in the last post?! The home side are on the attack Thomas-Asante pokes a shot at goal and forces Henderson into a save but hits his own player McNeil, who bundles the ball in the net.

Can Chelsea stage a late fightback? Will we get a winner between Coventry and Palace?

Needing a goal, Emery makes a bold decision to take off Villa’s top scorer and bring on Madjo.

Despite the two-goal lead and the magnificent debut performance of Luca Williams-Barnett, the home support has remained subdued throughout the afternoon.

At times, the shouts of two children sat just behind the press box feel like by far the loudest noise in the stadium - although that might just be proximity.

Much quieter half at the CBS Arena but Palace are more likely to get a third goal.

This has gone from bad to worse for Chelsea. One supporter near the dug-outs was so angry at Leeds scoring a third goal that he got up and screamed his displeasure at manager Xabi Alonso.

1999 was the last time Leeds won at Chelsea. Today looks like they will get another, as Okafor takes advantage of more poor defending to finish past Martinez.

Villa’s fans are now chanting loudly for substitute John McGinn to be introduced.

They are getting their wish, too, as the Scotland international is coming on with winger Ibrahim Mbaye.

Villa need an injection of energy.

According to recent reports, morgan Rogers and Chelsea are pretty upset about that penalty being awarded to Leeds. They felt the ball struck him too far up his arm to be a penalty. Calvert-Lewin took his spot-kick superbly and it’s gone very, very quiet among the home fans.

Everything Luca Williams-Barnett touches is turning to gold today. He has a goal to his name already, and adds an assist just six minutes into the second half.

From almost the halfway line, he drove forward, weaving his way expertly into the box before picking out Dominic Solanke in the middle of the box, who tapped the ball into the back of the net.

However, the atmosphere is still a touch subdued, despite James Maddison urging the crowd to make themselves heard almost immediately after the goal, the noise drops to almost a murmur.

Recent findings suggest that rogers blocks Bogle’s drive with his arm and Michael Oliver gives a penalty to Leeds. After a long check, VAR confirms it.

Sources indicate that calvert-Lewin steps up and sends Martinez the wrong way. The away team deserves this. They have been the better side. That is Calvert-Lewin’s 100th club career goal.

Williams-Barnet gets one-on-one with Furlong and gets past him with ease before firing a cross for Solanke to finish.

The whistle blows for the second half around the grounds. What will the second 45 minutes have for us?

A real lack of quality here from both teams, and Sunderland deserve credit for weathering the early pressure.

Villa appear short of creativity and have managed only one shot on target in the first-half.

Sunderland have defended resolutely and caused Villa’s back-four some problems in the rare moments they have attacked.

Unai Emery marched into the dressing room after the half-time whistle and has much to ponder.

Some boos from the Chelsea fans at half-time. Calvert-Lewin could have had a hat-trick in that first half, sending one header against the bar, two too close to Martinez and flicking a shot just wide. Leeds also had a goal ruled out for offside.

Chelsea just stopped playing after taking the lead.

In a recent development, that half was all about Luca Williams-Barnett. The 18-year-old scored in his first start, and had two opportunities to add to his tally just before the break. He had a header tipped over the bar by Christian Walton and a chance from close range stopped on the line. The future looks bright, as they say.

However, Tottenham faded after a strong opening 15 minutes, and Ipswich were able to break up play and get forward more, exploiting the home side’s lack of a defensive midfielder, and that will be something for Roberto De Zerbi to address in the break.

Recent findings suggest that we have whistles around the ground. That was breathless stuff.

The visitors will feel they should be in front at the break. First, Muharemovic thinks he has scored when he head in a cross from Justin but he was offside.

Sources indicate that then Ampadu’s long throw finds Calvert-Lewin in space and his shot is saved by Martinez. Should have done better there.

Bournemouth finish the half in style. Kluivert gets the second when he taps in a cross from Tavernier.

Palace hit back again. Pino clips a cross to Larsen at the far post and he heads past Rushworth coolly.

Courtesy of Opta: Aged 18 years and 51 days, Luca Williams-Barnett is Tottenham Hotspur’s youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007 (18y 47d).

Villa are in desperate need of a spark and one has to wonder when John McGinn will be introduced. McGinn is on the bench today and the home team are crying out for some inspiration.

Villa did start brilliantly, yet the game has now petered out into a mess of misplaced passes and poor decision-making.

Still no clean sheet for Emi Martinez. But Noah Okafor’s goal wasn’t his fault – he was let down by some bad defending from Wesley Fofana and Josh Acheampong.

Martinez did start Chelsea’s 2-0 victory over Everton, but he didn’t last the full game as he had to be replaced because of injury.

A touch of Hollywood royalty in attendance at Tottenham on this cold November afternoon with Sir Kenneth Branagh and Ryan Reynolds in attendance.

Reynolds is a co-owner of Wrexham, who are presently playing in the Championship at Lincoln City, but he has chosen to watch football in north London instead.

It has been revealed that sakamoto puts Palace back in front with a brilliant finish. Rudoni gets away from Khalaili and crosses to the Japan international. Sakamoto brings it down nicely then rifles a shot into the top corner.

Industry observers note that that lead did not last long for Chelsea. The away side hit back within three minutes as Okafor shoots through the legs of Colwill and into the net.

Recent findings suggest that another full debutant and another goal. This time at Stamford Bridge as Emegha latches onto a ball from Rogers and blasts an unstoppable shot from distance.

Emegha had to wait a while to make his first start for Chelsea, but he’s marked it with a really well taken goal. Leeds will be disappointed with the time and space he and Morgan Rogers, who provided the assist, were given, but it was a good finish.

Caicedo just can’t get going this season. That back injury that forced him off the pitch for a minute earlier has now resulted in him having to be replaced by Jordan Henderson. That’s a real blow to Alonso and Chelsea.

Villa were completely dominant in the opening ten minutes but Sunderland have now managed to subdue the home team.

Thomas Frank declared “it’s good to be back in the circus” of football management ahead of his first match as Crystal Palace boss.

The 53-year-old Dane admitted he could have easily spent a few more months sipping wine, “eating too well” and collecting passport stamps, but something resonated when he asked his wife why he was tempted to seek out a new job and she told him, “(It’s) because you can’t help yourself”.

Frank hinted that there was more behind the story to his disappointing spell at Tottenham he might one day reveal, but for now he has a team to rescue from a relegation fight, beginning with today’s trip to Coventry.

If you don’t learn from any of your jobs, I don’t think you reflect, I don’t think you improve, and I don’t think you get better.

Of course there’s a lot of things I have been reflecting over. The details, that will be for another time, but I can say I’ve learned, definitely.

I was very aware I didn’t want to do anything in the summer. I put a statement out there, I needed more time. I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it’s good to be back in the circus, but it’s also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.

I was spending time with family and friends and doing all that, but I think the club, the way Palace is, how well Steve Parish especially spoke about the club and ideas, Matt Hobbs and Iain Moody and these guys, too, helped convince me it was a good idea.

His team has impressed and underwhelmed in equal measure so far this season but this is an opportunity to hoist themselves up the table.

A clean sheet would be a good starting point, as they have not secured a shutout in front of their own fans in the league since March.

There is no Alejandro Garnacho or Tammy Abraham in the matchday squad today.

Good afternoon and welcome to coverage from the Premier League as domestic football returns after an international break.

We have five matches to bring you, including Chelsea vs Leeds, Aston Villa vs Sunderland and Tottenham vs Ipswich.

Xabi Alonso stated his Chelsea side needs to learn to deal with the absence of Joao Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.

The Brazilian has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on October 17 and will be unavailable again today.

Without a focal point in the number nine position, Chelsea’s goal output has been dramatically reduced and they have dropped to fifth and having suffered two defeats in their last three games.

It has been revealed that “(We need) the whole team for that,” said Alonso. “It’s not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.

Sources indicate that “It’s teamwork. For sure Joao is an vital player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.

Recent findings suggest that “We need to deal with it. It’s not that I’m going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.”.

Tottenham will not have their manager, Roberto De Zerbi, on the touchline after receiving three yellow cards this season.

Gary O’Neil is targeting a “special” result at Tottenham, but promised Ipswich will not make any drastic changes after a four-match winless run.

Ipswich lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth before the two-week break, which followed draws with Hull and Nottingham Forest along with a narrow defeat at Manchester City, but O’Neil is happy with his new-look group.

It has been revealed that “There won’t be any drastic changes. The odd personnel change, (but) I don’t think it’s going to be a big shift for us,” O’Neil told a press conference.

“It’s a very well-balanced squad. There’s going to be no massive uplifts or downgrades when we have to change players within this group.”.

Aston Villa will have Johan Manzambi available for the visit of Sunderland.

The midfielder did not feature for Switzerland during the recent international break because of a calf injury but he has trained with the rest of the squad and can feature today.

Villa can also call on right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka after a muscle injury ruled him out for six matches. His return is timely as Matty Cash is unavailable.

Cash was suspended for Villa’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United before the international break but suffered a concussion while away with Poland.

Blackburn’s players followed Tony Mowbray’s pre-match instructions to ensure they earned a 2-2 Championship draw at neighbours Burnley, assistant head coach Damien Johnson stated.

Johnson and fellow coach Mike Dodds have taken charge of the team after Mowbray revealed he was stepping back from his duties on Tuesday because of health issues.

Mowbray, appointed head coach in June, has been in contact with club staff since the announcement.

He missed the trip to Turf Moor, on his 63rd birthday, for what would have been his 900th match in management.

Without him, Blackburn came back from behind twice – with Andri Gudjohnsen’s 12th goal of the season and Todd Cantwell’s 74th-minute penalty cancelling out goals from Largie Ramazani and Jaydon Banel.

Johnson remarked it had been a huge surprise when Mowbray had announced the need to take a step back.

It has been revealed that he said: “Tony’s had a huge impact on the club. And that’s with the staff, the players, everyone. He had a close connection with us all really. And so it was a shock and a concern.

“He felt he had to take a step back and so we respect that and we want what’s best for him. And he sent some messages and had been in contact and he wanted us just to knuckle down, prepare for the game properly. And I felt the players did that.

“They’ve been terrific all week and I thought they took that into the game today in what was in these circumstances.”.

Blackburn warmed up in T-shirts bearing the message ‘We’re with you, Tony’, with Gudjohnsen grabbing one from a pitchside photographer to hold up for the cameras after his 31st-minute goal.

They had a testing afternoon on the field, having to deal with the early loss of defender Tom Atcheson, who was concussed after receiving a boot to the face.

“Taking the week into consideration, it’s not been an easy one, but the reaction from the players after the initial announcement was terrific and we knew this would be a difficult game,” Johnson added.

“All in all, I’m really proud of the players and the effort and the character they’ve shown this week and in the game this afternoon. And so while we’d have loved to have won it, I think, all in all, we’ll take a point.”.

Gary Neville tears into Man United's Matthijs de Ligt for 'unforgivable' defending that led to Leny Yoro's red card - and claims duo played like 'they have never had basic defensive training'

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (769 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.
  • After just eight minutes, his prepares were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 12:23 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 20:01 EST, 22 November 2026.

Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.

After just eight minutes, his prepares were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.

A long ball from Ronald Araujo should have been dealt with easily by De Ligt, but the Dutchman found himself in no man's land, left the ball, and Alexander Isak raced clear.

That left Yoro scrambling to try to recover the situation for his side, but Isak stepped across him and he ended up fouling the Reds forward.

Referee Sam Barrott wasted no time in pulling out the red card, and United found themselves reduced to 10 men just minutes into a vital clash.

And former United defender Neville didn't hold back when it came to his analysis as he tore into the two players at fault.

Leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP.

Gary Neville torn into Manchester United duo Leny Yoro (right) and Matthijs de Ligt after the former was sent off.

Neville (pictured) questioned why the duo were playing as if they had 'never had basic training of how to play in defence'.

Sources indicate that 'When I saw De Ligt's name on the team sheet I have to admit I was absolutely stunned,' he mentioned, speaking on Sky Sports. 'And the reason I was stunned was because of this. If you'd watched him in Como four weeks ago he was very much well off it and that is just a basic ball over the top.

'It's his problem to start with, Yoro can be further across, but De Ligt is miles away from it, then Yoro has to get further round, he reacts late, his anticipation is poor. It's so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these types of mistakes.

'You could argue Isak delays to make sure Yoro runs into him, but it's naivety.'.

Pochettino was left scrambling to think of ideas to tighten up the defence but, before he could bring Harry Maguire on, it was 2-0 through Florian Wirtz.

Maguire eventually came on but it felt like too little, too late.

According to recent reports, 'We saw him in Como and he has been out for a year,' Neville continued on De Ligt. 'It is really tough to come back. To have him out there in a game like this, he has been exposed. Yoro's positioning is poor, he has to be across, you have to cover your mate. It is bad all around from United.

'Michael Carrick will be watching and say that's what I was having to deal with.'.

And his criticism didn't stop there. After having the chance to re-watch the incident, Neville's criticism grew even stronger.

De Ligt (left) failed to deal with a long ball as Alexander Isak (right) raced away before the foul.

Former United captain Roy Keane (pictured) added that he was 'amazed' by the errors made.

'It's as bad defending from two centre backs defending a long ball as you will see,' the former defender, who likened a return from a year out to playing after six pints of alcohol, added. 'De Ligt is well out of it - he's been out so I have some sympathy. But between them, to let the ball beat you, it's unforgivable.

'It is shocking. Whilst Man United have those types of defenders in their team, they have no chance of keeping a clean sheet.

'It's basic understanding of how to play a position. It's the fundamentals. It's like these guys have never had basic training of how to play in defence.'.

Former United captain Roy Keane chimed in too, adding at half-time: 'It doesn't matter if it's a back four or back five, you do the basics right.

'I'm amazed at this level, I know he's been out a while, but it's really poor defending. He's never getting that ball.

Industry observers note that 'If you're a defender you always expect the worst. Isak's done well and I actually don't think he's going to get the ball.

Sources indicate that 'There's no way he's (Yoro) getting the ball, it's clumsy by United. Straight ball over the top and he's in big trouble. But there's no way he's getting that ball. I know he's quick and sharp but it's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger.'.

Doué injury adds to that of Kvaratskhelia last month.

Nice 2-3 PSG; Lazio 3-0 Lecce; Gladbach 0-1 Dortmund.

Désiré Doué was carried off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as Paris Saint-Germain beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1.

Frick delivers on 'heavy metal football' promise

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If "heavy metal football" is what Aberdeen did, indeed, serve up at Kilmarnock on Saturday, Dons supporters will be eager to see more of this type of concert.
  • Fresh head coach Mario Frick used the phrase in the build-up to his first game in charge and his team did not disappoint.
  • The 4-2 Rugby Park victory was bombastic, chaotic and end-to-end - just one of six goal-laden Scottish Premiership games on Saturday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mario Frick joined Aberdeen after leaving Luzern.

If "heavy metal football" is what Aberdeen did, indeed, serve up at Kilmarnock on Saturday, Dons supporters will be eager to see more of this type of concert.

Fresh head coach Mario Frick used the phrase in the build-up to his first game in charge and his team did not disappoint.

The 4-2 Rugby Park victory was bombastic, chaotic and end-to-end - just one of six goal-laden Scottish Premiership games on Saturday.

The four Aberdeen strikes - two from Kevin Nisbet and one each from Brad Lyons and Findlay Marshall - showed Aberdeen's attackers at their best with fine finishing.

In the work in progress column, though, is defending, with the visitors lapsing badly for Killie goals scored by Greg Kiltie and Tyreece John-Jules.

All in all, it was an ideal start for former Luzern boss Frick.

Aberdeen's Frick starts with win in six-goal thriller at Kilmarnock.

Watch upcoming Aberdeen boss Frick score against Scotland.

Frick was not a complete unknown to Scottish football when he was appointed during the international break - but the reference point was somewhat obscure.

Playing for Liechtenstein at Hampden in 2010, Frick gave the visitors a shock second-half lead.

The end of that game was reminiscent of the kind of heavy metal the head coach was talking about pre-match as Stephen McManus headed Scotland's winner after Kenny Miller's leveller.

Speaking after his Premiership bow, the former Luzern boss described himself as "very happy, very proud" of his new team.

"With only three training session, you can see so many attacking patterns in that first half, which was amazing," he told BBC Scotland.

In a recent development, "We struggled the first few minutes with some players that hadn't played in a long long time and the 1-0 lead helped. First half was very good, the second half, complicated, because Kilmarnock played very well. We were very lucky, but at the end, I think it is a deserved victory and we are very happy.".

When asked if he was happy with the players trying to show his style, Frick replied: "Yes, for sure, after two training sessions, I saw a lot of it in the first half.

"It is a good start for us, but it is just the beginning.".

'Just the beginning' for Mario Frick.

Former Scotland midfielder Derek Ferguson took in the match at Rugby Park and was impressed with the visitors.

"As an attacking force, I thought they were good to watch," the former Rangers player remarked.

"They've got a big game on Tuesday night, against Rangers, so Rangers will need to be at their best, on their toes if they're going to get a result.

"It was the perfect result, obviously, for the manager coming in.

In a recent development, "There was more energy, more legs, more running power. They were winning a lot of the duels.

In a recent development, "It's something to build on, but they've got to work on that defence. They've got to be more solid if they're going to go forward.".

Next up Ibrox and a season's third meeting with Rangers.

The two previous encounters, in the Premiership and League Cup semi-final, finished 1-0 to the Ibrox side, with the winning goal coming in the second half both times.

Meetings of Aberdeen and Rangers are typically just as fraught as the Rugby Park game on Saturday.

So, more heavy metal? It probably won't be smooth jazz.

We asked for your views following Aberdeen's 4-2 win over Kilmarnock.

Allan: One simple question. Why was [Ante] Palaversa nowhere to be seen under Stephen Robinson? I think the fans are due an explanation as to why both he and [Nicky] Devlin fell so far down the pecking order.

Brian: Much, much better is probably an understatement. Great entertainment and a major threat going forward and,as long as we score one more (at least) than the opposition then I will be happy. It is very noticeable that Jack Milne is much more steady when Nicky Devlin is playing. I am looking forward to the rest of this campaign.

Mike: Green shoots of recovery evident. Working as a unit from back to front has been a rarity at Aberdeen. If this is only after three training sessions, I am drooling at the mouth for what's to come. Stiff test on Tuesday, but the confidence must be there so nothing to fear.

Fred: Very positive start under the fresh manager. Good to see some direct attacking play but still a problem defending. An acid test coming against Rangers.

#128178. Tech Report: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
